answer:
You're missing some &&s in that command.

RUN pip3 install --upgrade pip && \
    pip3 install -I dbt-core==1.8.2 && \
    pip3 install -I dbt-postgres==1.8.2 && \
    #(... etc ...)

Otherwise, that command is interpreted as

pip3 install --upgrade pip
pip3 install -I dbt-core==1.8.2 pip3 install -I dbt-postgres==1.8.2 
# (...etc...)

– hence pip complains it can't find a package called pip3 to install (or, following that, a package called install...). You can replicate that in a regular session with:

$ pip3 install -I dbt-core==1.8.2 pip3 install -I dbt-postgres==1.8.2
Collecting dbt-core==1.8.2
  Downloading dbt_core-1.8.2-py3-none-any.whl.metadata (3.9 kB)
ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement pip3 (from versions: none)
ERROR: No matching distribution found for pip3

However, it'd be better to just install everything you can in a single pip3 install invocation:

RUN pip3 install --upgrade pip && \
    pip3 install -I dbt-core==1.8.2 dbt-postgres==1.8.2 # ... etc ...
